question.text: Why do many Cat I/II AIFs prefer to pay Incentive Fee ONLY AT END OF FUND TENURE (or after major exits), rather than annually on NAV growth, per Chapter 6?

answer.text: SEBI prohibits annual incentive fee payments for Cat I/II funds
Annual incentive fees attract higher GST
To avoid 'double-counting' incentive on the same gain as NAV moves up-down-up, and to accommodate future loss-provisioning through clawback
Annual payment requires daily NAV computation, which Cat I/II cannot do

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Chapter 6 conclusion to Example 6.3: annual incentive computation causes DOUBLE COMPUTATION of incentive on the same excess return (Y1 excess already earned carry; Y2 increase on top includes the Y1 base again). End-of-tenure payment solves this and also accommodates future NAV decline via clawback safety. **The Trap:** A is false (not prohibited); C mis-applies GST; D confuses reason (Cat I/II CAN do NAV, they don't want to do ANNUAL CRYSTALLISATION). **Cross-Exam Context:** Same mechanic in XIX-C. Cat III (XIX-E) pays HWM-crystallised carry periodically — different construction. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** If you must pay annual carry (LP insisted), model the double-count carefully and build a 'look-back true-up' at year 3 and fund end. Otherwise GP over-earns on paper and ends up in a clawback shortage.
